industry: Aerospace & Defense — Submarines, Combat Vehicles, Munitions, Business Jets, Government IT
thesis: General Dynamics is the most backlog-secure of the US defense primes after the July 2026 Navy award handed Electric Boat $71.6B for five Columbia-class and nine Virginia-class submarines, lifting company backlog 32% YoY to a record $136.5B. All four segments booked above 1.0x in Q2 2026, Gulfstream is finally converting its order book into deliveries at 14.5% segment margin, and management raised FY2026 guidance to $16.80-$16.90 diluted EPS on ~$55.7B revenue. Yet the stock sits near its 52-week low at ~19x forward EPS because a Middle East de-escalation narrative has compressed the whole prime-contractor group — a dislocation between a contracted, decade-long production backlog and a sentiment-driven multiple.

financials.gross_margin: 10.2% (operating margin; GD does not report a gross margin line)

drivers: Submarine production ramps on schedule: the $71.6B Electric Boat award de-risks Marine Systems revenue into the late 2030s and Marine margin keeps climbing off the 7.3% Q2 2026 level
Gulfstream sustains a 1.3x-plus book-to-bill and delivers 165-plus aircraft annually, holding Aerospace margin above 14.5%
GD-OTS munitions and the seven-year Pentagon interceptor framework agreement turn artillery and missile-component replenishment into a durable growth line
Free cash flow conversion returns to 100% of net earnings, funding a 35th consecutive dividend increase plus larger buybacks
Defense primes re-rate back toward 24-25x forward EPS as the peace-dividend narrative fades

assumptions: FY2026 lands inside guidance at ~$55.7B revenue, 10.5% operating margin and $16.80-$16.90 diluted EPS
FY2027 EPS reaches ~$18 on high-single-digit revenue growth as backlog converts
Multiple holds at 21-22x forward EPS — roughly GD's five-year average, below the 2025 peak
Capex stays elevated near 3.5-4% of sales to fund shipyard and Gulfstream capacity, capping near-term FCF upside
Dividend grows ~6% annually and share count drifts lower via buybacks that more than cover dilution

risks: A durable Middle East and Ukraine de-escalation triggers a full peace-dividend de-rating of the primes to 16-17x forward EPS
Submarine build-rate shortfalls or shipyard labour constraints push cost growth onto GD under incentive-fee terms
Business-jet demand rolls over with a macro slowdown, stalling the Aerospace margin story that has driven recent upside
FY2028 budget pressure or a Pentagon acquisition reset compresses Technologies and Combat Systems award flow
Continuing-resolution or shutdown dynamics delay obligations and push unbilled receivables higher

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 earnings and call — first read on submarine award ramp, Gulfstream deliveries and FY2026 guidance confirmation
FY2027 defense appropriations progress — determines shipbuilding and munitions top-line visibility
Q4 and FY2026 results plus initial FY2027 guidance; historically also the annual dividend-increase decision window
FY2028 President's Budget request — first look at post-reconciliation shipbuilding and combat-vehicle profiles
Incremental Navy, Army and GDIT awards; NATO and European rearmament orders for Combat Systems

key_risks: Geopolitical de-escalation compressing defense-prime multiples regardless of contracted backlog
Concentration in US government customers and exposure to appropriations timing, continuing resolutions and shutdowns
Fixed-price and incentive-fee shipbuilding contracts carry cost-overrun and schedule risk at Electric Boat
Skilled-labour and supply-chain constraints in submarine and munitions production capacity expansion
Business-jet cyclicality — Aerospace is the highest-margin segment and the most macro-sensitive
Elevated capex near 3.5-4% of sales suppresses free cash flow conversion while capacity is added
